question: In an early build of your support agent, the agent has five tools: get_customer, lookup_order, process_refund, escalate_to_human, and a generic update_account tool that accepts any field name and value. Logs show that the agent sometimes changes credit limits when customers ask, although policy lets it change only contact details. A system prompt rule against such changes reduced these cases but did not stop them. What is the most likely root cause of the remaining changes?

options.text: The agent holds too many tools, so the added decision complexity makes it choose update_account when a more suitable tool exists for the customer's request.
options.reason: The agent has only five tools, which is within the 4-5 range that the guide treats as reliable, and the failure is the content of the call, not the tool choice.

options.text: The update_account tool returns its errors without the isError flag, so the agent cannot see that its attempted changes to restricted fields have failed and keeps retrying them.
options.reason: The forbidden changes succeed, so the problem is not hidden errors; the generic tool accepts the restricted field and applies the change.

options.text: The tool_choice setting is "auto", so the model may answer with conversational text when the customer's request should have produced a call to update_account instead.
options.reason: The "auto" setting only decides whether the model calls a tool; the failure here is a tool call that writes a restricted field, which tool_choice does not control.

options.text: The update_account interface accepts any field name, so only a prompt rule that the model follows probabilistically stands between a customer request and a forbidden change.
options.reason: A generic tool puts no constraint on its inputs, so prompt guidance is the only barrier; a constrained alternative that validates its inputs would block these changes.
